questions.help: Road traffic collisions     8 The rule - PAHCorrect behaviour in the first 10 minutes directly after a collision is of vital importance as it:Saves lives. Avoids further collisions. questions.help: Road traffic collisions                 8 The rule - PAH    8.2 Advise: Request for helpBefore requesting help you should make a quick assessment of the scene. questions.help: Road traffic collisions                          12 Recognition of non vital signs (secondary evaluation)      12.2 BurnsBurns can be severe so you should know the correct behaviour for treating all types of burns:- Don’ touch the burnt area –this alleviates the risk of infections.Apply cold water (never apply any ointment).Treat the burn without removing any clothes –as these maybe stuck to it.Apply a damp, sterile bandage.(Página 266 del manual 'Learning to drive')Road traffic collisions                        12 Recognition of non vital signs (secondary evaluation)     12.2 BurnsBurns can be severe so you should know the correct behaviour for treating all types of burns:Elevate and maintain elevated, the burnt region, where this is possible and the burnt area is on an extremity, as this will help to reduce swelling.Excepcionally you can give a drink of bi-carbonated water to the victim, but only once you have established there are no other injuries; the patient is completely conscious and isn´t vomiting.- Don’ let burnt surfaces touch.- Don’ cut or burst any blisters, as it can infect the wound.(Página 266 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: Road traffic collisions                      12 Recognition of non vital signs (secondary evaluation)       12.1 Haemorrhages 12.1.3 Visible haemorrhages (from the orifices) Haemorrhage from the nose or the mouth:As the case before, treat the victim with extreme care. Never plug these hemorrhages.(Página 266 del manual 'Learning to drive')
questions.question:
Ante un motorista accidentado con una hemorragia por la nariz, la actuación correcta es...
An injured motorcyclist has a nosebleed, the correct way to act is...

answers.text:
Inclinar la cabeza hacia delante y taponar la hemorragia.
Lean the head forward and plug the haemorrhage.

Inclinar la cabeza hacia atrás y taponar la hemorragia.
Lean the head backwards and plug the haemorrhage.

No taponar la hemorragia, en ningún caso.
Never plug the haemorrhage.

questions.help: Road traffic collisions                      12 Recognition of non vital signs (secondary evaluation)       12.1 Haemorrhages 12.1.3 Visible haemorrhages (from the orifices) Haemorrhage from the nose or the mouth:As the case before, treat the victim with extreme care. Never plug these hemorrhages.(Página 266 del manual 'Learning to drive')
questions.question:
De las que a continuación se citan, ¿qué actuación es correcta ante un herido que presenta una hemorragia por la nariz?
Which of the following is the correct behaviour when administering first aid to a person bleeding from the nose?

answers.text:
Sí, pero nunca una distancia mayor de 50 km.
Yes, but never over a distance greater than 50 km.

Sí, siempre que no haya otro medio.
Yes, provided there is no other option.

No, en ningún caso.
No, never.

questions.help: Road traffic collisions 13 Transferring casualtiesAlways, whenever possible, await the arrival of an ambulance with persons and doctors adequately trained. Only in exceptional cases should you transfer casualties to the nearest hospital. For example:In an isolated area with no chance of asking for and receiving assistance.If the help is delayed for over 30 minutes and the casualty presents a progressive state of unconsciousness with symptoms of shock or a severe haemorrhage, that continues to bleed profusely and can’ be stemmed or it has been necessary to place a tourniquet on the casualty(Página 267 del manual 'Learning to drive')Road traffic collisions   13 Transferring casualtiesAny transfer of the casualty should be done using a lorry or van, so you can place them in an adequate position and at the same time it is possible to have a person next to them to carry out resuscitation if necessary and calm the victim.During the transfer the driving should be soft, at an adequate speed for the state of the road and volume of traffic so as not to aggravate the injuries.(Página 267 del manual 'Learning to drive')
questions.question:

answers.text:
Es obligatorio dependiendo del número de pasajeros transportados.
It is compulsory depending on the number of passengers transported.

No, un botiquín es solamente recomendable.
No, a first aid kit is only recommended.

Sí, es obligatorio.
Yes, it is compulsory.

questions.help: Road traffic collisions  14 First aid kitsAlthough it is not obligatory, it is recommended that you have a first aid kit in your vehicle that contains the following essential items:Disposable gloves.Sterile cotton dressings.A cervical protection collar.Bandages, compresses and sterile gauze.Band-aids (plasters).Scissors, safety pins and tweezers.Piece of elastic 5 to 10 cm wide and at least 150 cm in length.A mask for resuscitation.(Página 267 del manual 'Learning to drive')
